get.description: Verifies `state`, requires the `activity:read_all` scope, exchanges the code for tokens, stores the athlete with encrypted tokens and enqueues the initial backfill. If the login carried an allowlisted `return_to`, the browser is redirected (303) there with `connected=1`, or with `connect_error=<reason>` once the state itself is valid.

400.description: Bad state, denied access, missing scope or bad code

get.description: Redirects the browser to Strava's authorize page with a signed, expiring `state`. An optional `return_to` that exactly matches `OAUTH_RETURN_TO_ALLOWLIST` is signed into the state; after the callback the browser is sent there. Any other value is ignored.

parameters.description: Where to send the browser after connecting (allowlisted URLs only)
parameters.name: return_to

schema.description: Where to send the browser after connecting (allowlisted URLs only)
schema.title: Return To

get.summary: Readiness: PostgreSQL and Redis are reachable

get.description: Stored activities of all active athletes (or one, with `athlete_id`), newest first. Soft-deleted activities are excluded. Pages are keyset-based: pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor`. Rows inserted while paging never shift or repeat a page.

parameters.description: Start date ≥ this (UTC if no offset)
parameters.name: from

schema.description: Start date ≥ this (UTC if no offset)
schema.title: From

parameters.description: Start date < this (UTC if no offset)
parameters.name: to

schema.description: Start date < this (UTC if no offset)
schema.title: To

get.description: One stored activity of an active athlete, by its Strava id. Unknown and soft-deleted activities are 404.

Count, distance, moving time and elevation for activities whose start date falls in `from`..`to` (both inclusive, UTC days), the same totals per sport type (sorted by sport type), and the longest activity: the one with the greatest distance, the newest on a tie. An empty range gives zeros, an empty `by_sport` and a null `longest`. Defaults to the last 12 weeks. Soft-deleted activities are excluded.

Count, distance, moving time and elevation per ISO week (Monday start, UTC) for activities whose start date falls in `from`..`to` (both inclusive). Weeks without activities are returned with zeros. Defaults to the last 12 weeks. Soft-deleted activities are excluded.
Latest backfill and incremental run per active athlete, webhook intake and retry counts, current Strava rate-limit usage, and the circuit breaker state of every process that talks to Strava.

put.summary: Record body weight for a day

get.description: Built-in and custom exercises by name. `q` matches name or slug (case-insensitive substring), `muscle` the primary or a secondary muscle, `equipment` any of the given.

post.description: The slug is derived from the name; a name whose slug exists already is `409`.

get.description: Per workout that logged the exercise (oldest first): best set, best e1RM (Epley, 1-12 reps), working volume. `from`/`to` are inclusive UTC dates.
Every program, newest first, without days.

post.description: A program with its days (in order) and planned exercises (in order). The program generator's preview (`POST /programs/generate`) has a `program` field that can be sent here unchanged. New programs are inactive.

400.description: A planned exercise does not exist

get.description: The one active program with its days, or `404` when none is active.

delete.description: Deletes the program and its days; logged workouts stay.

get.description: One program with its days and planned exercises.

put.description: Replaces name, goal, weeks and all days. Logged workouts stay; their link to a replaced program day becomes null.

400.description: A planned exercise does not exist

post.description: Makes this the only active program (idempotent).

get.description: Standing records per exercise: heaviest weight per rep count, best e1RM and best session volume, with the workout that set them.
Working sets and kg (reps x weight) per ISO week and primary muscle. `from`/`to` are inclusive UTC dates; default the last 12 weeks.
Newest first, keyset-paginated (ADR 0009): pass `next_cursor` back as `cursor`.

post.description: Starts a workout, free or from a program day. The response lists the day's planned exercises with the last performance of each (working sets of the most recent other workout that logged it).

delete.description: Deletes the workout and its sets.

get.description: Sets, volume, records hit and (for a program day) the plan with last performance.

post.description: Sets `ended_at` (default now); an empty workout can be finished. Finishing again keeps the first `ended_at` (idempotent) but updates `notes` when sent.

delete.description: Idempotent: deleting a set that is not there is also `204`.

put.description: Upsert by the client-generated `client_id` (ADR 0017): the first call creates the set (`201`), a retry or a correction with the same id updates that same set (`200`, same body for the same input). Retries and double taps never create a second set. An id already used in another workout is `409`.

get.description: Strava calls this once when the subscription is created. Echoes `hub.challenge` when `hub.mode=subscribe` and `hub.verify_token` matches `STRAVA_WEBHOOK_VERIFY_TOKEN`.

post.description: Validates the event, stores it once (deduplicated on subscription, object, aspect and event time) and enqueues `process_webhook_event`. Always answers 200 for a well-formed event, including duplicates and events for another subscription, so Strava does not retry. No Strava call happens here.

400.description: Body is not a valid Strava event
